newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast CARB gas up on buying interest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast CARB gas up on buying interest.

text.p: U.S. West Coast CARB gasoline prices rose in light Friday trade amid talk that refiner in San Francisco bought heavily yesterday, traders said.
A flurry of CARB gasoline cargoes sold in the Bay area, including a 50,000 barrel supply to ARCO, traders said.
Refineries continued to ramp up from planned maintenance, with higher output reflected in last week's 91 percent plant capacity figure, a 1.2 percentage point from the week before.
Meanwhile, trading activity faded as players left early for the weekend, or business meetings.
Traders expected prices to fall next week when four full cargoes arrive on the West Coast.
CARB gasoline in San Francisco was assessed between 70.50 and 71.50 cents a gallon, up two cents from Thursday levels.
Los Angeles CARB rose 1.50 cents a gallon from yesterday to 71.50/72.50 cents.
Distillates, meanwhile, were flat to lower in line with a weaker New York Mercantile Exchange and rumors of CARB diesel cargo due in next week.
CARB diesel was talked two cents lower at 74/75 cents a gallon, while jet fuel unchanged around 64 cents.
West Coast gas stocks remained tight, at 26.9 million, or 2.3 million barrels below a year ago, according to weekly reports published by the industry and government.
